name: Digital arrest (fake police / CBI / ED / customs on a video call)
how_it_works: A caller poses as police, CBI, ED, NCB, customs or TRAI. They say your Aadhaar, SIM or a parcel is linked to a crime, show fake warrants or ID cards, keep you on a video call for hours, tell you not to tell family, and ask you to move money to a 'verification' or 'RBI safe' account.
red_flags: Threat of immediate arrest
Video call with someone in uniform or a fake police station background
Told to stay on the call and keep it secret
Asked to transfer money 'for verification' or to 'clear your name'
Official-looking warrant or letter sent on WhatsApp
official_facts: 'Digital arrest' has no basis in Indian law. No police or agency arrests or interrogates people over a video call.
No agency asks you to transfer money to prove innocence.
Real summons are served in person or by post, not on WhatsApp.
what_to_do: Disconnect the call now. You are not under arrest.
Do not transfer any money or share bank details.
Call a family member, then call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

name: Courier or parcel scam (FedEx, DHL, Blue Dart, India Post)
how_it_works: A message or call says your parcel is held: either it 'contains drugs or passports' (then the call is transferred to fake police, leading to a digital arrest), or it needs a small 'redelivery' or 'address update' fee paid through a link that steals card details.
red_flags: A parcel you never sent
Call transferred to 'police' or 'customs'
Small fee via a link
Link domain is not the courier's official site
official_facts: Courier companies do not transfer you to police.
India Post does not ask for redelivery fees through SMS links.
what_to_do: Do not press 1 or follow the call transfer.
Track parcels only on the courier's official website or app.
Do not enter card details on links from messages.

name: Electricity disconnection threat
how_it_works: A message says your power will be cut tonight because the last bill was 'not updated'. It gives a personal mobile number of an 'electricity officer' who asks you to install an app or pay a small amount, then takes over the phone or steals bank details.
red_flags: Deadline of tonight
Sent from a personal 10-digit mobile number
Asked to call an 'officer' or install an app
official_facts: Electricity companies do not send disconnection threats from personal mobile numbers.
Bills can be checked on the official discom website or app.
what_to_do: Do not call the number or install any app.
Check your bill on the official discom app or website.
Block and report the number on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu).

name: Bank KYC / account-blocked scam
how_it_works: A message claims your bank account, YONO or card will be blocked unless you update KYC/PAN or redeem reward points through a link. The link is a fake bank page that captures your login, card number and OTP.
red_flags: Threat that the account will be blocked today
Link that is not the bank's official domain
Asks for OTP, PIN, CVV or full card number
APK file to install
official_facts: Banks never ask for OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords by message or call.
Banks do not ask you to update KYC through SMS or WhatsApp links.
Indian banks are moving to the exclusive '.bank.in' domain, which only RBI-verified banks can register.
what_to_do: Do not click the link or share any OTP.
Call the number printed on the back of your card or visit your branch.
If you entered details, call your bank to block the card and call 1930.

name: UPI 'enter PIN to receive money' / QR / refund scam
how_it_works: Someone says they sent you money by mistake or are paying for something you sold, then sends a QR code or a 'collect request'. Scanning or approving it and entering your UPI PIN sends money out of your account.
red_flags: Asked to enter UPI PIN to receive money
Pressure to approve a request quickly
Screenshot of a payment you can't see in your bank app
official_facts: You never need to enter your UPI PIN or scan a QR code to RECEIVE money.
Entering the UPI PIN always means money is leaving your account.
what_to_do: Decline the request. Do not enter your PIN.
Check your bank balance in the bank's own app, not a screenshot.

name: Investment / stock-tips / trading app scam
how_it_works: You are added to a WhatsApp or Telegram 'stock tips' group, then asked to install a trading app that shows fake profits. Withdrawals are blocked until you pay 'tax' or 'fees'. These scams caused about three-quarters of cyber-fraud losses in India in 2025.
red_flags: Guaranteed or very high returns
Unknown app not on official stores
Must pay to withdraw your own money
Group admins posing as SEBI-registered advisers
official_facts: SEBI-registered advisers can be checked on the SEBI website.
No genuine broker asks you to pay fees before withdrawing your money.
what_to_do: Stop sending money, even to 'unlock' withdrawals.
Exit the group and report it.
Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 with all payment details.

name: Part-time job / task scam
how_it_works: An 'HR' message offers easy money for liking videos or rating hotels. Small payments arrive first to build trust, then you are asked to deposit money for 'prepaid' or 'merchant' tasks that never pay out.
red_flags: Unsolicited job offer on WhatsApp or Telegram
Pay to earn
Earnings shown only on a website you can't withdraw from
official_facts: Genuine employers do not ask you to pay to get work.
what_to_do: Do not deposit any money.
Block the sender and report on cybercrime.gov.in.

name: APK file or screen-sharing app scam
how_it_works: You are sent an .apk file (for example a 'wedding invitation', 'RTO challan' or 'PM Kisan' app) or asked to install a screen-sharing app. Once installed it reads your SMS OTPs or lets the scammer control your phone and empty your bank account.
red_flags: An .apk file sent on WhatsApp
Asked to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer or similar
Asked to give an app permission to read SMS
official_facts: Government departments and banks do not send apps as .apk files on WhatsApp.
what_to_do: Do not open or install the file.
If installed, turn on flight mode, uninstall it, and call your bank and 1930.

name: Fake customer-care number
how_it_works: A fake helpline number listed online or sent in a message offers to fix a refund or complaint, then asks you to fill a 'refund form', share an OTP, or install a screen-sharing app.
red_flags: Helpline number from a search ad or social media comment
Asks for OTP or app install to process a refund
official_facts: Get helpline numbers only from the company's official app or website.
what_to_do: Hang up. Contact the company through its official app.
Do not share OTPs or install apps.

name: Lottery / KBC / prize scam
how_it_works: A message says you won a lottery, KBC prize or lucky draw and must pay a processing fee, GST or 'income tax' to claim it.
red_flags: Prize for a contest you never entered
Fee required to receive the prize
official_facts: Genuine prizes never require you to pay a fee first.
what_to_do: Do not pay anything. Block and report the sender.

name: Family emergency / voice-clone impersonation
how_it_works: A caller or message from a new number claims to be a relative (sometimes with an AI-cloned voice) or says your child has been arrested or hurt, and asks for money urgently.
red_flags: New or unknown number
Extreme urgency
Asked not to call anyone else
official_facts: Police do not demand money over the phone to release someone.
what_to_do: Hang up and call the family member on their known number.
Agree on a family code word for emergencies.

name: Fake buyer or 'army officer' marketplace scam
how_it_works: Someone posing as an army or CRPF officer offers to buy your item or rent your house, then asks you to send a small amount first or scan a QR code 'to receive' their payment.
red_flags: Buyer agrees without seeing the item
You are asked to pay to receive money
Army ID card photo sent as proof
official_facts: You never pay money to receive a payment.
what_to_do: Accept payment only into your account without entering any PIN.
Do not scan QR codes from buyers.

name: Fake traffic e-challan
how_it_works: A message says you have a traffic fine and links to a lookalike payment page or an .apk file.
red_flags: Link is not on the official parivahan.gov.in site
APK file attached
official_facts: Official e-challans are checked and paid on echallan.parivahan.gov.in.
what_to_do: Check the challan only on the official Parivahan site.
Do not install apps from the message.

name: Pension / EPFO / life-certificate scam targeting seniors
how_it_works: A caller says your pension will stop unless you update your life certificate or bank details, and asks for an OTP or Aadhaar details.
red_flags: Threat that pension stops today
Asks for OTP, Aadhaar or bank details on a call
official_facts: Life certificates are submitted through Jeevan Pramaan, your bank branch or authorised centres, not by sharing OTPs on calls.
what_to_do: Do not share OTPs. Confirm with your bank branch or pension office directly.
